articleTitle: IEE Colloquium on 'Software in Computer Networks' (Digest No.10)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Software in Computer Networks
IEE Colloquium on Software in Computer Networks
abstract: Summary form only given. This paper gives an overview of one manufacturer's proprietary network software (SNA) and compares its development and implementation with that of the Open Systems Interconnection standards. The objectives of SNA and OSI are different; SNA provides network services (hierarchical and peer-to-peer) within an IBM network, while OSI permits interworking between networks from different manufacturers.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A review of the ISO application layer protocols
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Software in Computer Networks
abstract: The ISO Reference Model for open systems interconnection (OSI) provides a structured framework into which standards relating to OSI can be integrated. The ultimate aim of the various standards being developed is to establish a communications environment which enables application software running in computers from a number of different manufacturers to communicate in an open way to achieve a common distributed goal. An outline of the seven protocol layers is given. The author looks particularly at the application layer.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Software in Computer Networks
abstract: A brief history of the UK's activities in OSI conformance testing up to the beginning of 1986 is given. The remainder of the paper concerns the progress since then and the current status of the various activities. The author discusses standardisation, European OSI conformance testing services, the UK Consortium on OSI testing, the Corporation for Open Systems and accreditation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Software in Computer Networks
abstract: DAPES (data processing expert systems) was one of nine Alvey clubs aimed at stimulating the use of expert systems in British organisations. Two subject areas were chosen, a system to assist the running of a help desk and a system to assist network controllers with fault diagnosis. The author discusses these systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Formal methods applied to protocols-the Alvey FORMAP project
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Software in Computer Networks
abstract: FORMAP (formal methods applied to protocols) is a project within the Alvey Software Engineering programme, now carried out by British Telecom and GEC. It aims at both main goals of the programme: to develop improved methods and tools covering all roles and aspects of the life cycle to enable the professional software developer to produce improved quality and more cost effective software; to create an improved climate for the use and acceptance of the methods and tools that exist now and that will flow from the programme. Technically, the project aims to develop a theoretically sound approach to protocol engineering by using formal methods.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The systems approach to computer networks
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Software in Computer Networks
abstract: This paper is based on experience within the Ministry of Defence on the factors to be considered when creating an integrated system of communications and information systems for command and control of the battlefield. The Army has concluded that achieving integration of a complex network of communications and information subsystems requires far more than the implementation of ISO communications protocol standards. This wider view could well be necessary for other large networks.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
